summary:
BAIEF is a bilingual educational web application that places a real location on Earth beside a geologically similar landscape on Mars or the Moon at the same ground resolution. Students can compare landforms without misleading differences in zoom, explore live planetary imagery, and learn the story of the spacecraft, rover, lander, or lunar vehicle left at the distant location.

The project includes eight curated landscape pairs, six on Mars and two on the Moon. It also provides an exploration mode where students can select their own locations, explain the geological similarities, save their work, and export it as a file. BAIEF makes planetary geology easier to understand by connecting distant landscapes with places people can visit on Earth. It also preserves the stories of abandoned space hardware and turns scientific data into an accessible classroom experience.
